i-slint-core 1.18.1 from crates.io with one addition, in properties.rs (search for "Telescope patch"): PropertyTracker::evaluate_as_dependency_root_keeping_invalidation.

Why: the interpreter's geometry cache (vendor/slint-interpreter/PATCH.txt) uses a PropertyTracker per item. evaluate_as_dependency_root clears the tracker's dirty flag after running the
closure, so a property the closure itself invalidates after reading it (an item whose width makes a ComponentContainer create its component, which sets a property height read earlier) is
forgotten and the stale result is cached as clean. The new method clears the flag before running the closure, so is_dirty() afterwards says whether that happened.

Why a new method and not a change to the old one: evaluate_as_dependency_root has many callers that rely on the old order, or would at least change behaviour with the new one (a render or layout
pass that sets properties it read would stay dirty and ask for another frame forever). Callers in 1.18.1, all left as they were: PropertyTracker::evaluate and evaluate_if_dirty, item_rendering.rs
(scale factor), graphics/boxshadowcache.rs, window.rs (redraw tracker, popup trackers), properties/ffi.rs, the winit backend's accesskit.rs and the Qt backend's qt_accessible.rs. Only
slint-interpreter's item_geometry and its Instance::ensure_instantiated call the new method.

Measured together with the cache: see vendor/slint-interpreter/PATCH.txt.

Drop it together with the geometry cache, or when upstream's evaluate_as_dependency_root stops losing an invalidation raised during evaluation. Then remove this folder and the i-slint-core line
under [patch.crates-io] in rust/Cargo.toml. Tests, benches, the lockfile and the [[bench]] entry in Cargo.toml were left out of the copy. Slint's GPL-3 option is what Telescope uses; the licence
files are kept in LICENSES.
